transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-15, 16:30 UTC / Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz, Zoe Patel (Redwood) — Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, Hannah Wu, Marcus Bell, Sofia Marin (Apexbridge)

Auto-generated Summary:
- Kickoff for Redwood onboarding: network/VPC/connectivity, model routing, and benchmark plan.
- Primary goals: get Private/Dedicated deployment options validated for compliance and latency SLOs, confirm network changes, and schedule a perf benchmark.
- Action items captured and next steps agreed.

Topics detected: Onboarding scope; VPC and firewall; Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; Model quantization; Benchmarks and SLOs; Stakeholders and timeline

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right hello everyone, welcome. Thanks for joining. We're gonna run through the activation and integration kickoff for Apexbridge. Uh I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Rafael, our SE, and Zoe our CSM.
[00:14] Liam O'Connor: Hey Maya, thanks. Good to see everyone. Quick intro from our side — Hannah is our CTO, Priya is platform, Marcus SRE and I'm running ML ops. Sofia is PM.
[00:27] Maya Chen: Great, thanks. Goal for today: confirm network constraints, what scope we put in the pilot, and a rough benchmark plan. Rafael, wanna kick us off on the technical outline?
[00:38] Rafael Ortiz: Yeah sure. So the typical activation has three lanes — connectivity and VPC, model onboarding and runtime config, and load/perf testing. For Apexbridge specifically, you mentioned low-latency routing for short queries, is that right Liam?
[00:53] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, most calls are like 60–200 tokens, sub-200 latency is important. Cost is a secondary constraint. 
[01:04] Priya Desai: To add, we have strict egress policies — everything has to go through our NAT and we only allow specific IP ranges outbound. We also have an internal requirement for audit logs and using our KMS for key wrapping.
[01:18] Rafael Ortiz: Understood. We support VPC peering and private peering options, and for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS via HSM-backed flow. There might be a little bit of handshake work for the KMS — we usually hand over a key wrapping flowbook.
[01:33] Marcus Bell: Sorry just to interrupt, how do you handle token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tracing? Our ops needs to be able to attribute cost to each service.
[01:43] Zoe Patel: Yes we expose per-route token counts in the Console, and we can give you trace hooks to correlate request ids to internal traces. We'll also share a sample dashboard export for cost by model and route.
[01:55] Hannah Wu: On the security side, SOC2 and ISO were mentioned in the deck we saw. Can you confirm what evidence you provide — like audit logs retention and SSO integration?
[02:07] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We provide SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO attestation summary, SSO via SAML, and audit logs can be routed to your SIEM — we can retain logs for a configurable window depending on the plan. For Private installs we can ship longer retention.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: Cool. Can you talk through Dedicated vs Hosted? I know cost is important but we're leaning on predictable throughput.
[02:29] Rafael Ortiz: Sure — Hosted is fastest to start, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and guaranteed throughput, and you get the capacity isolation which helps with tail latency SLOs. There's also Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need full control. For latency-critical small requests Dedicated + small batch size is often ideal.
[02:47] Priya Desai: If we do Dedicated behind our VPC, what changes are we expected to make network-wise? Do we need a VPN, peering, or direct connect?
[02:57] Rafael Ortiz: We offer multiple options — VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or a private link. It depends on cloud provider and policy. We'll draft a recommended diagram for AWS with step-by-step.
[03:09] [Speaker 5]: Uh, quick question — how do you do KV cache for chat workloads? Do you persist that into our side or keep it ephemeral?
[03:19] Rafael Ortiz: Good question. Our KV cache is ephemeral in the serving runtime to preserve latency. For persistence we can integrate with your object store or a managed cache, but default is ephemeral and controlled by the runtime. There are also prefix caching options.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: That could be a problem for us if the cache needs to be shared across regions. We might have to evaluate the cross-region consistency trade-offs.
[03:44] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll add cross-region caching notes to the runbook.
[03:51] Priya Desai: On encryption: we need server-side encryption with our KMS and HSM for key wrapping — any blockers?
[03:59] Rafael Ortiz: No blockers, we have KMS integrations. For Private deployments, customer-managed KMS is standard. For hosted, we can do envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some plans.
[04:10] Sofia Marin: Timeline question — we need pilot in about two weeks, is that realistic?
[04:17] Maya Chen: Two weeks is tight but possible for a limited pilot if we get network access and a model artifact. Rafael, is that doable?
[04:24] Rafael Ortiz: If Priya can provide network details and permissions this week, and you provide a sample model container or weights, we can stand up a pilot in 10–14 business days. We may use a lightweight quantized variant to speed things up.
[04:39] Marcus Bell: Any specific model formats you prefer? We mainly use ONNX and some PyTorch exported states.
[04:46] Rafael Ortiz: We support PyTorch and ONNX, and have tooling to convert to runtime-optimized artifacts. If you have Transformer-based models we have a recommended conversion flow; I'll share the conversion checklist.
[04:57] [00:05:10] — small cross talk, agreement on artifacts to share —
[05:20] Priya Desai: I'll need to loop in our networking team — they'll want to see specific CIDR ranges and TTLs. Also we run cloud infra through an internal proxy so the egress IPs must be static.
[05:33] Maya Chen: We'll provide a sample CloudFormation and an allowlist of IP ranges that we'd need. For static egress we can discuss the private link option.
[05:44] Liam O'Connor: Success criteria for pilot — sub-200ms p95 on 100QPS for 100-token requests, and cost per inference in a target range. Also audit logs ingested to our SIEM.
[05:57] Rafael Ortiz: We'll instrument the benchmark to measure p50/p95, and provide token-level cost reports. We'll also run a small A/B with quantized model to show cost delta.
[06:08] Hannah Wu: Who's the primary contact for the pilot once it starts?
[06:12] Zoe Patel: Zoe will be your CSM and primary for onboarding cadence, Rafael will do technical lead, and Maya will own commercial/contracting.
[06:21] [00:06:30] — short silence —
[06:36] Priya Desai: Also compliance check — do you support tenant-level RBAC integrations with our IdP? We need fine-grained role controls for read/write ops.
[06:46] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, we have RBAC with SAML roles and can map group claims. For Private deployments we can do even stricter network-level access.
[06:55] Marcus Bell: What's the telemetry footprint? We need to make sure agent or SDK doesn't leak internal metadata.
[07:02] Rafael Ortiz: Telemetry is opt-in; we can limit telemetry to error and perf metrics only. Full request payload telemetry is off by default.
[07:12] Liam O'Connor: Pricing question quickly — what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated baseline?
[07:17] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated has a reservation with lower per-token unit cost. We'll send a pricing sheet with a couple scenarios for your throughput.
[07:25] Liam O'Connor: Cool.
[07:29] [00:07:30] Rafael Ortiz: On model quantization — for many of your workloads, switching to INT8 or 4-bit quantization reduces unit cost 2–4x while keeping quality within tolerance for short queries. We'll produce a recommendation specific to your model family.
[07:43] Priya Desai: Are there known regressions we should watch for with 4-bit?
[07:47] Rafael Ortiz: Mostly hallucination risk in certain generation tasks. We'll provide a small eval harness and a prompt set for regression detection.
[07:56] Hannah Wu: For the pilot we'll run our standard accuracy checks and you can run quality monitoring on top — is that integrated?
[08:04] Zoe Patel: Yup, Redwood Optimize can hook into your evals to raise regression alerts and tie them to prompt sets. We can run a demo of that in the next week.
[08:14] [00:08:20] — short note about sharing decks and links —
[08:30] Maya Chen: Quick logistics: we'll create a shared folder with onboarding docs, network templates, and the initial sprint board. We'll invite you there after the call.
[08:40] Sofia Marin: Great. Also, for procurement — we'll need a sample MSA and data processing addendum to start legal review.
[08:49] Maya Chen: I'll send a starter MSA and DPA; legal can ping our agreements contact.
[08:54] [00:09:00] Rafael Ortiz: One detail on benching — do you want internal traffic patterns simulated? For example your spikes during morning batch job windows?
[09:04] Marcus Bell: Yes we have diurnal spikes; we'll share a 72-hour request trace sample with QPS distribution.
[09:13] Rafael Ortiz: Perfect. We'll use that to set the batching and autoscale policies.
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: Another item — what's the fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is saturated? We need graceful degradation.
[09:26] Rafael Ortiz: We support fallback routing to a lower-cost variant or to Hosted model variants. You can set per-route policies for failover. We'll document for your use-case.
[09:36] Priya Desai: For network egress, do you require NAT gateway logs to correlate? Our security team needs visibility.
[09:44] Zoe Patel: We can surface request IDs and log correlation keys to tie into NAT logs. We'll send an example correlation guide.
[09:52] [00:10:00] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Quick ask — can we get a short runbook for incident response? Who do we call?
[10:01] Maya Chen: We'll provide on-call escalation for Dedicated customers — an SLA page with P0 and P1 contacts. For Hosted there's tiered support. I'll attach the escalation tree.
[10:11] Hannah Wu: Let's capture the decision matrix: pilot -> if meets p95 and audit requirements -> escalate to Dedicated reservation.
[10:19] Rafael Ortiz: Yes that's the standard.
[10:22] [00:10:30] — pause —
[10:35] Sofia Marin: Any blockers we foresee?
[10:38] Priya Desai: The main blocker is the network egress policy and static IP requirement. Also need legal to start on the MSA.
[10:45] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize the network artifacts this week so you can start legal in parallel.
[10:50] [00:11:00] Rafael Ortiz: I'll put together a tech-runbook and a conversion checklist for your model formats.
[11:00] Liam O'Connor: Great. On the perf benchmark, what metrics will you report?
[11:05] Rafael Ortiz: p50/p95 latency, throughput, token-level cost, failure rates and tail latency distribution. Also a delta for quantized vs full precision.
[11:16] Priya Desai: Can we get an expected heatmap of latency by region?
[11:20] Rafael Ortiz: Yes we'll include a regional breakdown and routing policy suggestions.
[11:26] [00:12:00] — small side conversation about seat counts and API keys —
[12:10] Zoe Patel: One onboarding note — we'll provision a sandbox tenant with two API keys for Apexbridge testing. Do you want separate keys per team?
[12:18] Marcus Bell: Yes separate keys for infra and ML team please.
[12:22] Zoe Patel: Noted.
[12:25] Hannah Wu: Anything else?
[12:28] Maya Chen: Final recap — Redwood will share: VPC templates, sample CloudFormation, KMS integration notes, conversion checklist, pricing scenarios, MSA + DPA, and a proposed benchmark plan. Apexbridge will share: network diagram, firewall rules, request traces, and model artifacts.
[12:44] Liam O'Connor: That covers it. Thanks everyone.
[12:48] Maya Chen: Thanks. We'll follow up with the documents and schedule the benchmark planning block.
[12:55] [00:12:56] — meeting ends.
